findings: SvekNode.appendLabelHtml/appendTd emit the fractional 3x3 plaintext grid and h central port now emitted by Rust. Fresh multiple-node, self-link, cross-group and direction/width cases pass, as do the four retained maker shields.

The native parser's first cell allocation failure followed by successful realloc stores an unterminated array, then free_html_label traverses uninitialized pointers. Fault-injection index 3 reproduces an AddressSanitizer SEGV against the exact helper translation unit. This is an allocation-failure path, not a normal-input crash in the shipped CLI.

htmllex.doInt uses strtol and then range-checks the integer. The helper uses strtod, requires the complete token, and range-checks before truncation. Exact DOT probes show WIDTH=1e2 means 100 here versus 1 in Graphviz; WIDTH=65535.9 is rejected here but truncated to 65535 externally, losing the native h port on fallback. Empty width is accepted here despite doInt rejecting it. These are distinct from the ordinary fractional cases that pass.

153 bounded malformed/truncated/numeric/ragged/duplicate-port/oversize-row probes have no non-injected sanitizer crash. Row/column maxima, fixed-cell centering and ordinary fractional grid node dimensions agree with external 16.1 on tested inputs. The parser remains a general native entrypoint, so passing 3x3 production examples does not excuse malformed-input or numeric-contract failures.

The shipping binary links only libSystem and libiconv on macOS; no JVM, external Graphviz, Expat or font-library dependency was introduced. This is host linkage evidence, not a claim that the macOS executable has literally no dynamic OS libraries.
record.bounded_repair_guidance: Make partial allocations cleanup-safe before exposing an array; implement doInt's exact numeric contract or deliberately reject the unsupported subset without claiming parity. Keep central-port geometry and non-class callers covered.
